skill.name: lark-workflow-meeting-summary
skill.description: Summarizes Lark meeting records for a selected date range and produces structured meeting reports with note and transcript links.
skill.summary: Create structured daily or weekly reports from Lark meeting notes and metadata.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick findings are markdown syntax, not Ruby execution. Several lark-cli command examples are real external-command behavior and should require user consent because they read meeting metadata and can write documents. The ../ links are real package-boundary filesystem reads, while the high-entropy alert is a false positive caused by normal markdown and Chinese text.

remediation.suggestion: Replace ../ skill links with packaged documentation or declared dependencies. Do not instruct agents to read outside the installed skill directory.
Require explicit user confirmation before running lark-cli commands, especially docs create or update. Quote arguments and reject shell metacharacters in user-provided values.
State the exact Lark domains and permissions needed before login. Avoid drive access unless document links or document creation are required.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time turning many Lark meetings into clear updates. This skill searches meeting records, gathers note links, and formats daily or weekly summaries.
actual_capabilities: Search Lark VC meeting records for a chosen date range.
Handle pagination and split long meeting searches into one-month ranges.
Fetch meeting note metadata and transcript document tokens by meeting ID.
Batch-query Lark Drive metadata to collect note and transcript links.
Format daily or weekly meeting reports with counts and meeting details.
Create a new Lark document or append the report when the user requests it.
limitations: Requires lark-cli and an authenticated Lark user account.
Only supports user identity workflows, not app identity workflows.
Search ranges over one month must be split into multiple requests.
Document links and document creation require Drive or Docs authorization.

use_cases.title: Prepare a weekly team report
use_cases.description: Collect meetings from the past week and turn them into a structured report with note and transcript links.

use_cases.title: Review daily meeting activity
use_cases.description: List meetings for a single day and identify which meetings have no available notes.

use_cases.title: Create a shared meeting archive
use_cases.description: Generate a Lark document that captures meeting titles, dates, note links, and transcript links for a date range.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize this week
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize my Lark meetings from this week. Include meeting titles, dates, note links, transcript links, and missing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a daily recap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a daily meeting recap for yesterday in Lark. Mark meetings without notes and group details by meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Build a weekly report
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a meeting weekly report for the past 7 days. Include counts, meeting details, links, and follow-up themes.

prompt_templates.title: Publish the report
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Lark meetings for last month, summarize them, then create a Lark document with the report. Ask before appending to any existing document.

output: The report starts with the total meeting count for the day.
Each meeting includes title, time, note link, transcript link, and missing-note status.
The report includes a weekly overview, meeting list, and available document links.
Meetings without notes are marked clearly so teams know which records need follow-up.

output_examples.input: Create a Lark document for last month's meeting notes.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a structured report and creates a Lark document after checking the requested date range and permissions.

best_practices: Confirm the date range before running Lark CLI searches.
Review Lark authorization scopes before fetching document links or creating documents.
Ask the user before creating or appending to any shared Lark document.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad date ranges without confirming the user need.
Do not create or update documents without explicit user approval.
Do not assume missing notes are errors; mark them as unavailable.

faq.question: Does this skill need Lark access?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires lark-cli and a user login for the vc domain. Drive access is needed for document links and document creation.

faq.question: Can it summarize any date range?
faq.answer: Yes, within Lark API limits. Searches longer than one month must be split into smaller ranges.

faq.question: Can it create a Lark document?
faq.answer: Yes, when the user asks for it and the account has Docs permission. It can also append to an existing document.

faq.question: Does it read full meeting note content?
faq.answer: The workflow focuses on meeting records, note metadata, and document links. Full content access depends on the linked document permissions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The workflow also needs the local lark-cli binary.

faq.question: What should users verify before running it?
faq.answer: Users should verify the target date range, account authorization, and whether a new or existing Lark document should be updated.
